semantic_atoms.claim: The exact archived wache-koenig source is a real pre-execution blocking gate for selected Bash commands when installed in a PreToolUse scheduler: it ignores non-Bash tools, classifies Bash command text, and returns the blocking exit path for hard-deny classes or ticket-required commands lacking a valid ticket.
semantic_atoms.boundary: Exact source capability is established; scheduler registration/order and current runtime reachability are not.

semantic_atoms.claim: The historical gate binds a grant to the exact command SHA-256, verifies validity timing, and unlinks the ticket on successful consumption, making the intended grant single-use rather than a reusable session-wide approval.
semantic_atoms.boundary: The ticket binds shell text, not resolved executable/resource/cwd/environment/generation identity; concurrent identical-consumption atomicity is unmeasured.

semantic_atoms.claim: The companion freigabe path requires a controlling /dev/tty and fresh human challenge responses before minting the one-shot ticket, preserving an architectural separation between model request and owner grant.
semantic_atoms.boundary: Typing heuristics are not identity proof and should not become EntityOS authority; the reusable invariant is out-of-model grant provenance, bounded scope, expiry and one-shot consumption.

semantic_atoms.claim: wache-koenig exits without enforcement for non-Bash tools by design. Therefore it cannot establish complete effect authority for Write/Edit/NotebookEdit or non-shell external effects, and current stern.py generic admission remains nonblocking bookkeeping.

architecture_deltas.delta: Frankenstein-2.0 must keep the strongest historical invariant: a model/candidate EffectRequest cannot self-authorize. A separately minted deterministic owner/capability decision is consumed at the real executor boundary before dispatch.

Replace raw-command tickets and caller skip_approval booleans with a one-shot typed EffectDecision bound to immutable invocation_id/tool_use_id, request_digest, resource identity, session/generation/causal identity, policy version, grant provenance, expiry and executor identity.

All state-changing tool/effect classes must converge on one deterministic enforcement adapter or explicit typed adapters with equivalent DENY=>nonexecution receipts. Bash-only regex gating is donor evidence, not complete authority.

contradictions.resolution: Exact archived wache-koenig.py and freigabe bytes/hashes are now resolved. Remaining unknown is exact scheduler registration/order and current/historical runtime reachability for that snapshot.

contradictions.claim_a: The historical watcher genuinely blocks selected Bash commands when installed.
contradictions.claim_b: It intentionally ignores non-Bash tools, while current stern generic effect admission is nonblocking.
contradictions.resolution_rule: Do not promote either mechanism to whole-system EffectGate authority. Triggerword-4 must implement typed cross-tool enforcement and prove DENY non-execution at the actual executor boundary.

hypotheses: The most reusable historical primitive is not the regex classifier but the separation model request -> independently minted bounded grant -> one-shot executor consumption.
Combining that invariant with current donor generation/precondition/idempotence checks and post-effect hashing yields a stronger causal EffectGate/EffectJournal design than either lineage alone.
counterhypotheses: A newer current host permission system may already supersede wache-koenig and cover more tools; exact source plus scheduler evidence could make it a better donor.
For shell-only execution a raw command hash may remain useful as a secondary exact-text fence, but it is insufficient as the sole typed resource/effect identity.
critical_unknowns: Exact historical/global settings.json or equivalent scheduler registration/order for this wache-koenig snapshot.
Whether current Frankenstein 0.7 uses this watcher, a successor, host permissions, or no equivalent gate.
Which current paths protect Write/Edit/NotebookEdit and Realtime function-call effects before external submission.
Atomicity of identical one-shot ticket consumption under concurrency.
acceptance_tests_feeding_triggerword4: DENY produces a bound enforcement receipt and zero executor dispatch.
One ALLOW/owner decision can be consumed exactly once for one immutable request identity.
Parallel identical or reordered requests cannot cross-consume decisions.
Bash, file mutation and Realtime/external effects share equivalent authority semantics.
After possible external submission, transport uncertainty becomes OUTCOME_UNKNOWN rather than cancellation or blind replay.
next_exact_gate: Recover exact scheduler/settings registration and ordering for the archived wache-koenig snapshot or explicitly quarantine runtime reachability; then trace current non-Bash and Realtime executor permission paths and feed the typed one-shot EffectDecision ABI plus DENY/nonexecution/concurrency tests into Triggerword-4.
